recognize_zh: 鐵染色（Prussian blue）下，紅色對比染色的有核紅血球母細胞胞質中有藍色含鐵顆粒，部分沿核周排列成環狀或半環，即環狀鐵粒母細胞（ring sideroblasts）。
features: Iron stain with red nuclear counterstain on bone marrow aspirate
Erythroid precursors containing coarse blue-green siderotic granules in the cytoplasm
Granules arranged in a perinuclear partial or complete ring in several erythroblasts
Scattered extracellular or background iron granules
Larger cells with pale nuclei (earlier precursors) lack granules
describe_en: Prussian blue-stained bone marrow aspirate shows erythroid precursors containing coarse blue siderotic granules. In several erythroblasts the granules encircle a substantial portion of the nucleus in a perinuclear ring. Individual granule counts per cell cannot be precisely assessed at this resolution. Findings are consistent with ring sideroblasts (defined as at least 5 granules covering at least one-third of the nuclear circumference).

ddx.vs: Normal sideroblasts contain only a few fine granules scattered randomly in the cytoplasm rather than a perinuclear ring.
Macrophage iron is clumped within large histiocytes with abundant cytoplasm, not in erythroblasts around the nucleus.
Precipitate lies in a different focal plane and is distributed randomly over cells and background.
